label: A sample also occupies space
before: Value stays at 0.95 throughout the field. You have varied one part of HSV while keeping two still. The gaps between columns contain possibilities that the collection has not put into a body. They are also where you can walk.
after: Value stays at 0.95 throughout the field. You have varied one part of HSV while keeping two still. The gaps between columns contain colours the collection has not raised into pillars. They are also where you can walk. Adding a column in one of these gaps would give another colour a body and take away somewhere you could stand.

label: A value meets different surfaces
before: Five columns by seven rows, with 3.2 metres between samples: the field gives the rule room to be walked. Each pillar rises 4.6 metres. Walk close enough to read a sample's address and colour code, then step back until several pillars overlap. The computed values remain fixed. What their company makes visible keeps changing.
after: Five columns by seven rows, with 3.2 metres between samples: the field gives the rule room to be walked. Each pillar rises 4.6 metres. Walk close enough to read a sample's address and colour code. Compare its surface with the floor at its foot. The floor displays its colour without the lighting applied to the pillars; the same computed value can meet you differently. Step back until several pillars overlap. Their values remain fixed. What their company makes visible keeps changing.

label: A collection has an author
before: Beyond the field, twelve collections hang on a framed wall. Their colours have names, and their groups have names too. These sets were assembled. The field was evaluated. Both are ways of deciding which colours belong together.
after: Beyond the field, twelve collections hang on a framed wall. Their colours have names, and their groups have names too: Bauhaus School Colors, Frida Kahlo's Palette, Harlem Renaissance Jazz. Someone has chosen which colours will stand here under those titles. The names suggest histories that these small lists cannot contain. These sets were assembled. The field was evaluated. Both are ways of deciding which colours belong together.

label: Carry a colour beyond its assigned company
before: Take a swatch if you want to carry that decision into another view. Its label pairs a hexadecimal RGB code with the nearest colour name from a small list. The code travels with it; its neighbours stay on the wall. Compare it with a pillar, with another swatch, with the space around your hand.
after: Take a swatch if you want to carry that decision into another view. Its label pairs a hexadecimal RGB code with the nearest colour name from a small list. The code travels with it; its neighbours stay on the wall. Compare it with a pillar, with another swatch, with the space around your hand. The label stays the same in this new company. Does the colour still look as though it belongs where you found it?
